newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Total 104m bbls Iraq oil okayed, more pending - UN.
newsitem.headline: Total 104m bbls Iraq oil okayed, more pending - UN.

text.p: The United Nations said on Tuesday that the total volume of oil approved under the "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq stood at 104 million barrels, with one contract pending approval.
As of last Friday, 37 contracts had been approved for a total volume of 104 million barrels, according to U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard.
Another U.N. spokesman said a 38th contract was pending and may already have been approved, though he couldn't confirm.

In his report to the Security Council on the first 90 days of the scheme, U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said that approximately 52.3 million barrels of Iraqi oil were expected to be exported in the first 90-day period, which ended on Sunday, March 9.
That total was expected to "be in the range of" the target of $1.07 billion for that period, which includes $70 million which Iraq is to pay to Turkey for pipeline fees.
That leaves 51.7 million barrels, or just over 574,000 barrels per day (bpd) approved for export in the second 90-day period, not including the pending contract.

However, though the volume approved for the second period is close to that lifted in the first, oil prices have declined around 20 percent since the start of the year. So, if current market prices prevail or go lower, a larger volume of Iraqi oil would be expected in the second 90-day period ending June 10, a U.N. official said.
